original_ci_failure.observation: CGO0 Linux caller-deadline returned Canceled/context canceled at displayed 0.25s; original CI did not record caller context cause or precise return timestamp.

code_level_proof: Server context uses context.WithTimeout for grpc-timeout.
An independent native timeout timer calls closeStream with RST_CANCEL.

closeStream invokes stream cancel before marking stream done. A concurrently awakened handler can therefore observe cancellation and attempt a Canceled trailer; this is a code-level possibility, not an empirically reproduced cause.
Client handleRSTStream normalizes expired RST_CANCEL to DeadlineExceeded, whereas native status trailers preserve their supplied status.

preserved_or_strengthened_oracles: Recv observer starts before opening the second RPC and records its terminal return timestamp.
Caller-deadline wire Canceled is accepted only with original caller context DeadlineExceeded and terminal timestamp at or after the original deadline and at most one second after it.
Initial-input-stall and idle-input-stall still require Canceled.
Original same-connection check, surviving mutation APPLIED confirmation, no replay and connection-open checks remain.
No production cancellation source is modified by this diff.
validation_limits: This is a source-only independent review; no Go tests or live backends were run for this review.
Prior public upstream loopback diagnostic: 1000 attempts, all DeadlineExceeded; no Canceled reproduction.
Prior existing Weir diagnostic overlay: 80 caller-deadline attempts passed; no Canceled reproduction.
Goroutine return timestamps measure observer execution time; they cannot prove instruction-level cancellation ordering under arbitrary scheduler starvation.
The local context check is an observed completion bound, not instrumentation of the internal runtime deadline timer.
